utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Good morning. Mr. Niemann, I understand that you wish to meet in camera this afternoon?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Yes, your Honours. It may be that it would facilitate a more free flowing discussion if we could meet in camera and discuss the question of the length of trial and so forth and what measures we have in mind. So, it is just a recommendation from us, if it is acceptable to the court.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Wladimiroff is not here. I understand he will be here this afternoon, Mr. Orie; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: That is correct, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Can we meet at 2.30 then before we meet this afternoon session, could we meet in camera?

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: I think there will be no problem because he is supposed to be here at 2.30.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: OK. Then we will meet in camera before we begin this afternoon's session. Mr. Niemann, would you call your next witness -- Miss Hollis?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, we would call Mr. Pasic. Your Honour, if the Prosecution could have Prosecution Exhibit 73? MR. EVIR PASIC, called.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Pasic, can you hear me? Would you take the oath, please, sir? Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Is that T-O-P-I-C?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: No, your Honour, it is Pasic, P-A-S-I-C.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth. (The witness was sworn)

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: You may be seated, sir. Thank you. Examined by MISS HOLLIS

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please state your name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My name is Elvir Pasic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is your date of birth?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was born on 7th October 1967.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is your ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Bosnian Muslim.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us your place of birth?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was born at Rogitica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that located in Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is it is in the eastern part of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, perhaps with the assistance of Miss Sutherland we could show Prosecution Exhibit 73? Could you please point to Rogitica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Perhaps we could zoom in on that for the court. Mr. Pasic, were you born in the town of Rogitica or in a village in the opstina of Rogitica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was born in the town of Rogitica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How far is Rogitica from Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Rogitica is some 66 kilometres away from Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did you live in Rogitica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: For a long time, 25 years.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Until what year?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Until mid 1992 when I left.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you know, could you tell us the ethnic composition of the area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the opstina of Rogitica, there was 66 per cent Muslim and 33 per cent Serbian population there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the town itself what was the ethnic composition?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the town of Rogitica there were 63 per cent Muslims and 35 per cent Serbs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To your knowledge, what was the JNA installation that was closest to Rogitica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The closest garrison of the JNA was at Han Pijesak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you point to that on the map, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (Witness indicates).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VOHRAH
utterances.text: Before you proceed, what is Zepa? Zepa represents the whole area there? You speak of the opstina of Rogitica ---

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VOHRAH
utterances.text: -- and that is where?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: It is the entire opstina within which you see the name "Rogitica".

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VOHRAH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Zepa is located within that opstina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VOHRAH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. (To the witness): Mr. Pasic, did you perform military service with the JNA?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was in 1986 and in 1987.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you perform that service?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was at Kraljevo in Serbia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were your duties in the JNA?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was in the military traffic police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During your service with the JNA, did you become familiar with JNA uniforms, ranks, weapons, equipment and markings?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us, in the military police are there any different uniform items or insignia worn by JNA military policemen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The military police had belts of white colour, and it had -- it wore on their sleeves white, other white covering on the sleeves and it had batons necessary for the performance of its duties.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This was in the performance of its traffic duties, the baton?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the military police wear any type of badge or insignia on their uniform?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We wore the emblem of the military traffic police, and of the barracks where we were located.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This white material on the sleeve, was this some type of cloth that you pulled over your uniform shirt sleeve?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we would mostly put it on our sleeves of the uniform when we were patrolling or when we were escorting military convoys.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the JNA uniform that you wore, what colour was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was grey, olive green uniform.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that the type of uniform that is sometimes referred to as the SMB uniform?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Pasic, after your active duty tour, did you return to Rogitica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you perform Reserve duty after completing your active duty JNA tour?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, in Reserve police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were your duties in the Reserve police?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was a Reserve policeman in the Reserve military police, and I was a private in the patrol.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How much time did you spend each year performing these Reserve duties?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I spent, roughly speaking, once or twice a year, one or two days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you perform these Reserve police duties?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At the town of Rogitica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While you performed these duties, what type of uniform did you wear?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I wore a uniform of a grey colour, the same as in a military uniform but it was in grey colour. It was very similar to the regular uniform of the regular policemen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the colour of the regular police uniform?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was of a light blue or a grey colour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you performed this Reserve duty, were you armed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At first I was not armed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The regular police, were they armed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What type of weapons were they armed with?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They had guns.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they have any type of automatic weapons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not at first.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: Can I ask a question? Does your evidence mean that the Reserve military police wore a different uniform from the regular military police? You have told us what the uniform of the regular military police was, I think.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The difference was because the uniform was of a different colour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may follow up on that? (To the witness): Mr. Pasic, you were in the active duty JNA as a military policeman and then you performed Reserve duties as Reserve policeman. As a Reserve policeman, were you attached to the JNA or to the police department?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was attached to the police force.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To your knowledge, soldiers who performed other functions such as artillery or infantry in the JNA, would they perform their Reserve duties perhaps with the JNA?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they would.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the time that you performed these Reserve duties, were you ever trained, did you receive any type of training, in addition to the patrol duties?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We had additional training that was usually just theoretical lectures, and then the next day there would be some practical exercises.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever perform this training at Han Pijesak?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did any of your friends perform training of any kind at Han Pijesak?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, most of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These were JNA Reserve members?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What types of military duties or areas of specialisation did they have?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They performed military duties, specialised in artillery, signalling, drivers of motorized vehicles or infantry duties.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In September 1991, were you called up for continuous Reserve duty as a policeman in Rogitica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I was. I was called up for that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After you were called up for this continuous police duty, how long did you perform this continuous duty?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I stayed there from September 1991 up until the end of March 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Once you began your duties as a full-time policeman, were you at that time issued a weapon?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I received a weapon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What type of weapon did you receive?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: An automatic rifle and 150 bullets for that particular weapon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So in September '91, the police now had automatic weapons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you perform these full-time duties?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mostly in the town of Rogatica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After you became a full-time police officer, what uniform did you wear?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I wore the same uniform as I wore when I was a Reserve policeman.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were your duties after this full-time call up?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My duties were exactly the same as that of a regular policeman, which meant patrolling the town, controlling the traffic, in case there were criminals, to take them to the police station and so on.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Excuse me, Miss Hollis. As I understand the testimony, Mr. Pasic has testified that he wore a grey uniform.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Pasic, did you wear a grey uniform when you were in the Reserve military police?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then when you were called up to be a regular policeman, in September '91, you continued then to wear that grey uniform; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Mr. Pasic, I believe you indicated that the regular police wore a blue uniform; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any other differences between the uniforms other than the colour?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Regular police wore caps on their heads and the Reserve police wore military caps, and the regular police had insignia marking their rank; whereas the Reserve police did not wear any kind of ranks, insignia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Drawing your attention to the end of 1991 or the beginning of 1992, during that time period, did you see any increase in JNA troops that were moving into the Rogatica area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I saw that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where would you see these troops?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Those troops were mostly located and were going towards the exit of the Rogatica town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What types of uniforms did they wear?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The military grey, olive green uniform.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is the regular JNA uniform when you were in the JNA?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. JNA uniform.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the spring of 1992, did you notice any increase in JNA equipment or weapons moving into your area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, in the spring of 1992, more and more often one could notice columns of JNA military that were going through the town and concentrate either in our opstina or the opstinas of Visegrad or Pale.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you use the map again, please, and point out to the court the direction of Visegrad and Pale?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is the Visegrad opstina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The direction of Pale was -- in that area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You indicated that you saw an increase in this equipment. What type of equipment did you see moving into and through your area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could see artillery equipment, that is, canons and tanks, armed vehicles, and all the soldiers had infantry weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These vehicles and equipment and weapons, did you recognise them as JNA?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Also directing your attention to the spring of 1992, did you become aware of the creation of any new Serb autonomous region near the Rogatica area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the spring of 1992 was founded the Serb autonomous region of Romanija which was located in the area of Pale, Sokolac and Han Pijesak; it also included the area of Rogatica in it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever hear any sort of public pronouncements as to why this Serb autonomous region was necessary?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Public explanation was that the Serb population in that area felt in danger, and that is why they had to organise an autonomous region for its protection.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who was making these statements that the Serbs felt threatened and in need of protection?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The town of Rogatica, such declarations were given by Rajko Kusic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who is he?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was the Commander of the Serb unit that had been formed in the area of our opstina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To your knowledge, at this time were there any groups in Rogatica that were threatening the Serbs in the area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was not aware that there had been any groups that were threatening or putting the Serbs in danger.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned -----

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Excuse me, Miss Hollis, may I ask one question? Mr. Pasic, you indicated that Mr., I do not know how to pronounce his name, was in charge of the Serb unit; what was the Serb unit, the Serb unit of what?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: I was about to get into that.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I am sorry. MISS HOLLIS (To the witness): Mr. Pasic, you mentioned this Serb unit in the area that Mr. Kusic was the head of, where was this Serb unit located?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That Serb unit could organise at the village of Gucevo 10 kilometres from Rogatica, and the headquarters of that Serb unit was in the village of Borika which is 18 kilometres away from the town of Rogatica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What type of unit was this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was an infantry unit that had about 500 people in it, trained for combat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you learn about this infantry unit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At that time, apart from working as a Reserve policeman, I also worked at a local restaurant where local population used to go, and most of the people who used to go there were Serbs, and they would tell me about how they organised that unit and how they were members of that unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The two towns that you mentioned, Gucevo and Borika, what ethnic group or groups lived in those two villages?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The ethnic group of those villages was mostly Serb.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did this infantry unit have weapons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they had weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What type of weapons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They had infantry automatic weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever see these weapons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I saw some individuals wearing uniforms and carrying weapons and going through town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you recognise those as JNA type weapons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The same type of weapons we used at the JNA.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To your knowledge, when was this military unit created?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That military unit was created in the summer of, sorry, spring 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You indicated that this Serb unit was located in Gucevo and had its headquarters in Borika; were there any check points along the roads to either Gucevo or Borika?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At first, there was a checkpoint in the village of Borika, at the entrance of the village of Borika.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any checkpoints leading to Gucevo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In March 1992, checkpoints were formed at the entrance of most Serb villages in the opstina of Rogatica and as well one going towards the village of Gucevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who manned these checkpoints?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Checkpoints were manned by the members of the Serb unit organised at Gucevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To your knowledge, did any one group have difficulty in going through these checkpoints?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Such checkpoints, the Muslim population was checked then. They mostly had problems going through those checkpoints.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To your knowledge, did the Serbs have similar difficulties going through these checkpoints?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, they had no difficulties whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Again talking about the spring of 1992, did you become aware of any distribution of weapons to inhabitants of your area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you become aware of?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I noticed JNA vehicles going to the area, that is, villages with Serb population, staying there for a while, two or three hours, and then leaving those villages.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any incidents in those villages after the JNA left?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When JNA left, one can hear shots from automatic weapons and from automatic pistols after the JNA left those villages; it was usually at night time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any other incidents that you were aware of?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, as I was on the Reserve police in Rogatica, among other things, I used to sentry at checkpoints at the exit from the town to control the licences, documents and vehicles. On one occasion, I stopped a vehicle with Kumanovo plates. There were five persons in it; four of them were uniformed and armed, and the driver was in civilian clothes. I knew all five of them in person. I asked the driver to give me the documents, vehicles documents. He did not have them, and I thus wanted to search the vehicle. When the driver opened, I could see some 50 machine guns, some hand grenades and quite a lot of ammunition for these weapons. I asked him where he was taking those and he was saying that he was taking it to the village of Borika to distribute them among the villagers. At that moment I decided that the best solution was not to cause any trouble but to let them through.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You indicated that you saw automatic weapons and hand grenades; in what part of the vehicle were these automatic weapons and hand grenades?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the luggage compartment at the back of the car.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You indicated that the licence plates on the car were from where?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The licence plates were from Kumanovo which is in the Republic of Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also indicated that you knew all five of these men in the vehicle. Who were these men?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: One of them was Rajko Kusic. I know the nickname of others; one was Slavisa, another one Lube, another one was Trisa and one was Miki.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you know these men?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They all lived and worked in Rogatica and we often saw each other in the town. They used to come to the restaurant where I worked.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were these men wearing when they were in the vehicle at the checkpoint?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The uniformed individuals had camouflage uniforms in grey, olive green and they had automatic weapons with them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any types of insignia or patches or badges on their uniforms?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They had emblems of the Republika Srpska or Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was that emblem of the Republic of Srpska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This emblem looked like a circle with the Serb three coloured flag in the centre, and along the circumference it said the Army of the Serb Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This three coloured flag, do you remember the colours in the flag?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Blue, white and red.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You indicated you let them go because you decided that, perhaps, that was wisest course of action. Why did you make that decision? What were you concerned about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At that moment I felt that my life might be in danger and I could not defend myself against possible danger. That is why I decided to let them through.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever see any similar type of deliveries to Muslim areas of the opstina of Rogatica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not see any such distribution.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In September 1991, when you were called to full-time duty as a policeman, how was the police department in Rogatica organised? How many divisions did it have?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The Police Force in Rogatica was made of regular policemen, criminal investigation police, inspectors, police and Reserve police called up at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The head of the police department in Rogatica, what was his ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was a Muslim.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was next in line below him in the chain of command?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mladen Vasiljevic, Serb by ethnic origin.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What has his position?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was a Commander of militia. He appointed people to various duties, sometimes went on duty with them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he have a deputy?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he had a deputy.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the ethnic group of the Deputy Commander?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Muslim.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The inspectors, what were there their ethnic group or groups?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At the time there were three inspectors in the police station; two of them were Serbs and one was a Muslim.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then for the lower ranking police who performed the day-to-day duties, what was the ethnic composition of that group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The ethnic composition of the force was roughly 60 per cent of Muslims and 40 per cent Serb.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the spring of 1992 what changes, if any, occurred to the structure of the police department in Rogatica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, in the spring of 1992 the police station in Rogatica was divided.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How was it divided?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was divided, that is, the regular police station in Rogatica was headed by all of the Serb police who worked at that station in order to organise the police station or the militia station of the Serb Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were they housed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were housed in the same building as the regular police of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then how was this division made?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The division was made by literally partitioning the police building in Rogatica in two parts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: By how, by putting up some kind of wall?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, a wall was erected through the middle, across the corridor of the building, dividing the building into two parts so that it was partitioned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After this split, did any Serbs remain in the regular police unit of Rogatica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I believe you have already indicated, but could you tell us again the name by which the Serb Police Force now referred to itself?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The Serb police of the Serb Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did they acquire the weapons that they used?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They appropriated the weapons they received as regular policemen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they have any type of vehicles that they used?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They appropriated two-thirds of the vehicles owned by the regular Police Force in Rogatica and used those vehicles.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To your knowledge, who authorised this split?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I know, the orders came from the so-called Serb autonomous province of Romanija and the division was specifically put through by Mladen Vasiljevic, the Commander of the police in Rogatica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did any of the Serb policemen tell you why this had been done?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did they say?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They told me that they had divided because they thought that the Serb population, the town of Rogatica, was in jeopardy and they needed a unit such as Serb police in order to defend their people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To your knowledge, prior to the split, had there been any armed clashes between Serbs and Muslims in the Rogatica area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To your knowledge, prior to the split had there been any attacks by non-Serbs on Serbs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did this new Serb Police Force mean in terms of where the police units worked and patrolled?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That new Serb Police Force patrolled around parts of the opstina and the town where the Serb population lived mostly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The regular police unit then patrolled what areas?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The regular units patrolled largely the town of Rogatica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After this split occurred in the police department, what changes, if any, did you notice in the uniforms that the Serb police wore?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The Serb police uniform was not uniform, that is, some of them wore camouflage uniforms of grey, olive green; some did not wear camouflage uniforms, but in light blue and grey colours; some of them had SMB military uniforms. The majority of them had black or dark blue berets. Those berets bore the emblems of the Serb Republic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did any of them continue to wear the regular blue police uniform?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, none of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After this split occurred, how long did you continue to work as a policeman?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On that same day when the police was divided, I left the duty, the post.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did you leave the police department on that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I left the Police Force because I felt I was in danger because, to be a member of the regular Police Force as a Muslim in a town where there were a number of armed Serbs, I thought was dangerous.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say that there were a number of armed Serbs. When did you begin to notice a number of armed persons in the Rogatica area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the spring of 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The Serbs that were armed, were they in military uniforms, were they in civilian clothing or both?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Both.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What types of weapons did they have?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They mostly had automatic rifles with ammunition to go with them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Either before or after this split in the police department, did you also see Muslims carrying weapons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In addition to the split in the police department, at the same time did you notice any other changes in the political structure of Rogatica, the creation of any other new departments?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, in the spring of 1992 the opstina of Rogatica was divided, that is, Serb members from the municipality organised the Serb opstina of Rogatica and, in the wake of this, the Crisis Headquarters of the Serb opstina of Rogatica was established.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you know, who was in charge of this Crisis Committee, Crisis Headquarters?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The Crisis Committee, Crisis Headquarters, there was Rajko Kusic and Tomo Veselinovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was Tomo Veselinovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was the President of the Serb Democratic Party in Rogatica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like to draw your attention to May of 1992. At that time what changes, if any, did you notice in your ability to get access to different radio and television channels and stations?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, in the latter half of May 1992 we could not receive television Sarajevo, the television of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and at that time we could receive only the television Belgrade, television Novi Sad, they are in Serbia, and television called SRNA with the seat with a centre in Pale.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you notice any changes in the radio reception?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the radio programmes we could receive mostly came from radio station Sokolac which was a Serb station, by and large.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the same time did you notice any changes in the type of programming that you received?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the programme we received mostly Serb, that is, Serbs who were threatened in Bosnia and Herzegovina, that they had to get together and mobilize and all those feared for the army service should join the Army of the Serb Republic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the programmes indicate on whose behalf this call for the Serbs to mobilize was being made?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, those calls were broadcast on behalf, in the name of the Serb Republic and the presidency and the President himself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That was who?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Radovan Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During this time that you were hearing these broadcasts, to your knowledge, had there been any attacks on Serbs in the Rogatica area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like to draw your attention to 22nd May 1992; was that the date that Rogatica was attacked?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What type of attack was it? What type of weapons were used?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Artillery, mostly anti-aircraft weaponry and infantry weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What parts of the town were hit with artillery?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mostly the central part of the town and those areas of the town inhabited by the Muslim population.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did this shelling of the town last?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The shelling lasted for seven days with very brief intermissions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During these seven days did you ever hear the sounds of aircraft in the area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I could hear the sounds of the aircraft.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you actually see the aircraft?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I could not see them because I was in the cellar of the building where I was staying for my personal security.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you would hear these sounds of aircraft, shortly after these sounds would you hear any other sounds?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I heard detonations. I do not think they were far from the centre of the town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You indicated that during this time period you were staying in a cellar of a building; what building was this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was the building where I lived, where I had my apartment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was there with you in the cellar?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were members of my family, and approximately about 40 persons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During this seven days that you were in this cellar, did you have any occasion at all to come up from the cellar and see what was happening in the town?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During this time, did you see any military weapons or vehicles entering into the town?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Every day during the brief intermissions, tanks and APCs went through the town and they fired at buildings in the town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you recognise these tanks and APCs as JNA type weapons and vehicles?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After this seven-day period, were there any orders or ultimatums given to the population?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there were orders.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How were these orders given?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Those orders were given over loud speakers in the Serb part of the town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What orders were you given?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The order was that the entire Muslim population in the town was to come out to the central square in the town to be notified, to be advised, about their further behaviour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the people come out to the square?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Most of them did come out to the square.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened after you gathered there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Military, an APC came to the same square. It carried seven to eight armoured, uniformed individuals, two in civilian clothes and one of those armoured and uniformed individuals was a captain.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know this person?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He was a captain in what, the active duty JNA or the Reserve JNA?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was a Reserve JNA captain.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What type of uniforms were he and the others wearing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was wearing the conventional JNA uniform and other uniformed persons were wearing camouflage uniforms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that there were seven or eight uniformed persons; were there any others with them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were two persons in civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know the two civilians as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you know, what was the ethnic group of these uniformed persons and the two civilians?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were all Serbs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At that time were you given any demands or orders?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The Muslim population was demanded to sign loyalty to surrender, to move to the secondary school building so as to ensure their personal security until the town was cleansed of Muslim fundamentalists, extremists and green berets.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At this time, to your knowledge, were there any green berets or extremists in the town of Rogatica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On this occasion did you go to the school?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you go?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I returned to my apartment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Two or three days later, do you recall any further broadcast?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: During the next two or three days, the same appeals were repeated over the loud speakers in the Serb part of the town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During this time period were you aware of any armed resistance in the Rogatica area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I know, in the town of Rogatica itself there were about 50 persons with personal weapons who offered resistance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were these people Muslims?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What type of weapons did they have?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Their weapons were mostly personal weapons. They were pistols or hunting rifles.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like to direct your attention to 7th June 1992; on that date were you arrested?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did that happen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That day the shelling of the town was very intensive, so that most of inhabitants, most of the dwellers, in my building had to go down to the cellar; I was one of them. Around 7 o'clock in the evening, soldiers, Serb soldiers, broke into that building, into the cellar, and ordered us all out. Then they separated men from women. Men had to lie down on the ground facing the ground, and women stood some five or six metres away from them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When they ordered you out, did everyone come out of the basement shelter?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, there was one lad who did not leave the cellar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened after all you came out and the one young man stayed behind?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, one of the Serb soldiers threw a hand grenade into the part of the cellar where that lad was and when he screamed, that young man came out, he was covered in blood and injured.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You indicated that when you came out you were separated, women going to one side, men to the other. When you came out, did you see any other people who had also been gathered?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, in that same place there were about 10 of men and as many women and children brought out from another part of the building, that is, another entrance into my building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Of the people that were with you in the shelter and these other people you saw gathered outside, do you know what their ethnic groups were?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were all Muslims.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You indicated that the men were forced to lie down. What happened then after the men were lying down?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: While we were lying down, most of the soldiers who had captured us began to beat us, kick us with their feet, with their rifles and demanding that we surrender our weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have any weapons in your possession as you were lying there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I was lying on the ground. I did not have any weapons on me but in my flat was my personal pistol.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did any of the other men lying on the ground surrender weapons as they were being kicked or beaten?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: None of the other men had arms so they could not surrender.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These men who brought you out of the basement and then the men who were involved in kicking and beating the men lying on the ground, did you know any of these people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I knew most of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you recognise them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Most of them wore masks on their face, but I recognised them because of their voices and the names they called each other, and some of them did not even wear masks on their faces.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What types of clothing were these men wearing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Some of them wore a multi-coloured patched camouflage uniform.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What colours in this camouflage uniform?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Some of them wore grey, olive green camouflage uniform and some of them wore a blue camouflage uniform, light and dark blue in colour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Prior to this date, had you seen these light and dark blue camouflage uniforms?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Such uniforms were worn by some of the policemen of the Serb police in the town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You indicated that either by their voices or by actually seeing their face you knew most of these men. The ones that you knew, what was their ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Serbs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Once they brought you out, did they make any demands of you, of you personally?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Me personally, they asked weapons which I had while I was a police officer at Rogatica. I did not have such weapons, but I admitted I had a personal weapon. That was a pistol that was in my flat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they make any type of threats to you at this time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: One of them wanted to kill me. He wanted to cut my throat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he actually have a knife?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was the knife when he was making this threat?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Threatening me, the knife was in his hand under my neck.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you go to retrieve your pistol?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who accompanied you to do this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: With me went one of the soldiers who was masked, wearing a mask, and I recognised him so that I asked a cigarette off him while we were going towards my flat because I was convinced that once I will give them the weapon, they would kill me. When I asked for the cigarette, he said I have no reason to worry because he knew me. I recognised his voice. He was Vlado Markovic who used to work as an active duty policeman at the police station at Rogatica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he confirm that he was Vlado Markovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The group of you who had been brought from the basement and this other group of people who were already outside the apartment building, where were you taken from the apartment building area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After I surrendered my weapon, with my mother, my grandmother and my aunt, I was taken to the secondary school, the secondary school building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were these other persons from the apartment building taken there as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 10 minutes before I was taken there, women and children were taken from in front of the building, and all the men continued to lie down on the ground and their arms were tied with wire.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were taken to the school, how were you taken there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Escorted by two Serb soldiers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you arrived at the school, were there other people there who were being detained?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Apart from the women and children that had been captured in my apartment building, there were some other families there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know any of these people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I knew them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was their ethnic group or groups?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Two Muslim families there; a Serb family; one from a mixed marriage and one that I could not tell whether they were Muslims or Serbs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long were you held at the school?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A couple of days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the time you were held at the school, did you see any persons taken out for interrogation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. People were taken out for interrogation on several occasions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know any of these people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were their positions in the community?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Several of them were engineers, they worked as engineers; two of them were doctors; some were workers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was their ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (Answer not audibly translated).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Without mentioning any name or names, while you were at the school, did you see any woman or women taken from your room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How often did this happen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It happened every night.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: By whom was the person or persons taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were taken by Serb soldiers that were mostly in charge for -- there for our protection in the secondary school.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When the woman or women were brought back, what did you observe about their demeanour or behaviour?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They would not want to talk to anybody. They were concerned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These soldiers that would take them out at night, what types of uniforms did they wear?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were olive green in colour and the uniforms worn by the Serb police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know any of these people, any of these men, who took the woman or women out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was their ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Serbs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While you were at the school, did you see anyone other than the regular guards enter the school?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, one day I noticed three young men enter the school.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were they wearing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Trousers, grey, olive green; they wore t-shirts, black t-shirts, and red berets.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they carrying any kind of weapons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sniper rifle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say a "sniper rifle", what do you mean?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: ... sight so that you can see the target and that is easy to hit them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When they came in did you see where they went?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They went to the third floor in the physics classroom.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After they went into the classroom did you hear anything?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I heard shots.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then after that, did you see the three men again?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they left the school building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On this day that these three young men came to the school building, did anything else occur in the city that you were aware of?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, on that same day one-third of the town was burned down.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What part of the town was this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Part of the town where mostly Muslim population lived.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How were you able to see that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could see that because we were allowed to go to the third floor to the same physics classroom where from you could see the whole town, mostly the whole town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the time you were at this school, were you able to see any other military activity in the town?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. From a nearby hill in Rogatica, very often two to three tanks would fire on the town. In front of the school building there was a tank that was firing at the town every day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you recognise these tanks as JNA tanks?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you leave the school?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On 27th June 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many others, if any, were taken with you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That day some 200 people were taken away, men women and children.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were any left behind at the school?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, some 50 people were left behind.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know these people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were their occupations?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Some of them were doctors, some were engineers, some were workers, for example, plumbers, electricians, garage mechanics, and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These ones that remained behind, what was their ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Muslims.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Those who went with you of those that you knew, what was their ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (Translation not audibly recorded).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anyone tell you why your group was being taken away?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Kusic came that day to the school with his body guards and he told us that we were going on what he called "free territory", that is, the territory of central Bosnia, which was mostly controlled by the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: Can I interrupt for a moment? I did not get the response to the question: "Those who went with you, what was their ethnic group?" I see it is not on the transcript either.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Sorry, your Honour. Could you tell us, please, the ethnic group of those who went with you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were all Muslims.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were taken from the school how were you transported?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Transported with civilian buses and civilian trucks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have any escorts with you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you recognise these escorts?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they were members of the Serb militia which I knew from earlier on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you refer to the Serb militia what are you referring to by "militia"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When I say the Serb militia, I mean the same, the same police that split up from the regular police and which founded this Serb militia or police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were taken from the school where were you taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was stopped. We were told that all the men aged between 16 and 65 had to get down, and when we left those vehicles the convoy continued and 28 men, we were taken to an agricultural farm near the town, on the outskirts of the town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These other people who continued on, did that group include your mother, grandmother and aunt?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This farm that you were taken to, how long were you held there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I stayed there up until 15th July 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While you were there, how many other people were being held there?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That same 28 who were taken off the bus?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. They were the same 28 people that got off the bus and there were also three people that we could not see, but we knew they were there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you guarded while you were at the farm?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know any of these guards?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, those were mostly people that captured us. They guarded us at the school and they escorted us there. I knew most of those people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After this 20 days that you were held at this farm, where were you taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was taken to the Susica camp near Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How were you transported there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was transported on civilian buses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have any type of escort?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we had escorts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know any of these escorts?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (Translation not audibly recorded)

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: I am sorry, I did not get that answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We knew them all. Yes, I knew them all.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What was the ethnic group of these escorts?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Serbs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What uniforms or what clothing did they wear?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Camouflage uniforms of olive grey green colour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they have any type of insignia or patches on their uniforms?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Serb Bosnian Republic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On your trip between this farm and the camp of Susica, was the bus stopped?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we were told that we would be going to Kladanj to be exchanged, but the bus stopped at a crossroads at the junction between Vlasenica, Kladanj and Sehovici, a place called Tisce.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened when the bus stopped?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At the junction was a checkpoint and two soldiers came on the bus that personally reminded me of Chetniks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was it about them that reminded you of Chetniks?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As I knew in the second, what, in the Second World War the Chetniks looked like; these also had long beards, were dressed in a very untidy way, they were drunken and carried arms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What types of clothing were they wearing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: SMB uniforms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When they entered the bus, what did they do?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were swearing, threatening us that they would kill us straightaway and they wanted us to get off the bus.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they use any type of ethnic slurs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did they say?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They swore at our Turkish, Muslim, balija mother.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you arrived at Susica, how long did you remain there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At Susica I stayed one night.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you taken from Susica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was taken to the camp Batkovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How were you taken there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Transported on a civilian bus.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have any escorts with you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know of any of those escorts?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were they from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: All of them where from Rogatica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was their ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Serbs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How were they dressed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Some of them wore grey, olive green military uniforms, some of them wore the grey, olive green camouflage uniforms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they have any type of patches or insignia on their uniforms?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Some of them had patches of the army of the Bosnian-Serb Republic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long were you held at Batkovic camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: One year and five days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The guards at the Batkovic camp, during the year that you were there, what type of uniforms or clothing did they wear?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Some of them wore grey, olive green military trousers, and the same type of shirts, but were unbuttoned and dirty. Some of them wore grey uniforms, they were really wearing civilian clothes and some of them had a combination with sneakers and military trousers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you first arrived at Batkovic, to your knowledge, who was the Commander of the camp there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The Commander of the camp was a man named Vejlo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long was he in command while you were at Batkovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was a Commander for some three months.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What type of clothing did he wear?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Trousers and grey, olive green shirt and he wore a green beret ---

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he wear any type of rank -----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: -- a red beret.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he wear any type of rank insignia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Corporal, a JNA corporal.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that a JNA corporal or a JNA sergeant?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Lance corporal.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the treatment that you received while he was in charge of the Batkovic camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (Translation not audibly recorded).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I did not get any translation.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I have not either; the question was: "What was the treatment that you received while you were (sic) in charge -- while you were in the Batkovic camp".

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: While Veljo was in charge.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: While Veljo was in charge, what was your treatment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were treated very badly.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: During the time that Veljo was in charge, did you see any persons die as a result of their treatment in the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you see?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: One night some 10 guards from the camp took out a person they called "professor", I think he came from the area of Bijeljina. He was beaten the whole night through and Veljo was with them. In the morning when dawn broke out, I saw that the man was dead.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see anyone else killed while you were in the camp while Veljo was in charge?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, in the same way two elderly men were killed, and a man was killed because he was shot at.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who were the people who beat these men and who was the person who shot at the other men?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: These were mostly the guards that guarded the camp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say "mostly", who else was involved?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I said "mostly" because the access was allowed to the camp to all the soldiers that would come in the area, any one of them could come to the camp and beat anyone of the prisoners.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These soldiers who had come from the outside, what types of uniforms would they wear?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (Translation not audibly recorded).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am sorry. I did not get the translation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They wore grey, olive green camouflage uniforms, so grey, olive green camouflage uniforms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they wear any type of insignia or patches on these uniforms?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Some of them had the emblems with a cross and four letters "S".

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had you seen that emblem before?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think that was the emblem of the Serb Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. I think that is where I saw that emblem.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In addition to these people, did any non-Serbs in the camp take part in the beatings or abuse?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Two men whose nicknames I know and I know they were Muslim.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were their nicknames?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: One was called "Spajzer" and the other one was called "Pike".

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After Veljo left the camp, did the treatment improve at the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, slightly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the beatings continue?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, but less, less frequently.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the time you were at Batkovic, were you forced to perform any duties outside the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What types of duties were you required to perform?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the first line, front line and I was cutting trees.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were digging trenches at the front line, how would you be taken to this area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: While I was digging trenches, and that was at Majevica, we were located at the town of Lopare, and from there we were taken on military trucks to the place where we worked.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How were you taken from Batkovic camp to Lopare?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Military trucks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The persons who took you from the camp to Lopare, were they camp personnel, camp guards?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who these people were who transported you from the camp to Lopare?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Those were the people who lived in the village of Batkovic, that was nearby, near the camp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How were these people dressed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (Translation not audibly recorded).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I do not believe there was a translation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Grey, olive green military uniforms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the time that you were digging these trenches at the front line, was there any type of fighting going on?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there any firing towards the areas where you were digging trenches?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, every day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the time that you were at Batkovic camp, or at these locations where you had to perform these duties, were there any kinds of songs that you were required to sing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they requested.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who made the requests for this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was requested by camp guards or soldiers who came to the camp from time to time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What types of songs did they request that you sing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They requested us to sing mostly Serb national songs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall the lyrics of any of those songs.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Without singing it, of course, could you tell us what the lyrics of some of those songs were?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, "Who says who lies that Serbia is small".

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had you heard these songs before?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In what context or where would you have heard them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the spring of 1992, as I was a Reserve policeman, I could hear such songs on the premises -- in facilities in public facilities held by people of Serb origin.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
