utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Yes. Do you have a new list of exhibits?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, we do. Perhaps I could present that to the court as well?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: May we have it? It would be easier for us to follow. (Document handed). Does the Defence have a new list of exhibits?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, we have given a list of exhibits this morning. I did not recognise the document that was being handed to the witness. Perhaps if they can be identified so that we can try to track them as we are going through.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Do you have a new list of exhibits?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, we have been given a list of exhibits this morning. I did not recognise the document as being handed to the witness. Perhaps if they can be identified, so that we can try to track them as we are going through.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Do you have a list of exhibits starting at 74 ---

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: --- through 126? That is what I was referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, we do.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Very good. Does the witness have a document in front of her that has not been marked?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour, I apologise for that.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: We have decided that what we are going to do now is before you present it to the witness, have it delivered to the Registrar; ask the Registrar to mark it for identification purposes -- this might sound familiar to you -- and then once it is marked for identification purposes, then the usher will hand it to the witness and the witness then can refer to it by exhibit number. It helps, that is for sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Dr. Greve, do you recognise that document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is resolution 780, 1992 of the Security Council.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that the resolution which established the Commission of Experts?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would tender this exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: That is Exhibit 74, it should be?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Any objection to Exhibit 74?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Exhibit 74 will be admitted. MR. TIEGER (To the witness): Dr. Greve, in October 1993, were you selected to serve as a Commissioner on the United Nations Commission of Experts?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you begin your work on the Commission with any predetermined view of what had happened during the conflict in former Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As a result of Resolution 780, which has just been admitted into evidence, was information from international humanitarian organisations made available to the Commission?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That was information concerning the conflict as a whole?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The conflict as such and the specific allegation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like to ask you about some of the materials which prompted the Resolution and which were made available at the outset of the Commission's work. Could I ask that the next document be marked for identification as Exhibit 75? (Document handed). Dr. Greve, do you recognise that document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is a statement made by the President of the International Committee of the Red Cross at the opening of the international meeting on humanitarian aid for victims of the conflict in the former Yugoslavia which was held under the auspices of the United Nations High Commission for Refugees at the end of July 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that among the materials to which Resolution 780 refers and which was made available to the Commission at the outset of its work?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I believe it was made available immediately, but I was not a Commissioner from the Commission start, so I am unable to say exactly when it was made available.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it made available to you at the outset of your work?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I tender that as the exhibit next in order Exhibit 75.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Any objection to 75?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: The Prosecution's Exhibit 75 is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Can that document be placed on the monitor, your Honour?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Dr. Greve, can I ask you to turn to page 1, the fourth paragraph? In that document did the President of the ICRC report to the Commission that, "... whole populations are being terrorised, minorities intimidated and harassed, civilians interned on a massive scale, hostages taken and that torture, deportation and summary executions were rife in the former Yugoslavia"? I would ask you to look at paragraph 4 of the document.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do. I am sorry if I missed the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that the report in part by the President of the ICRC that was presented to the Commission?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the President of the ICRC further indicate that all of that was done in the name of ethnic cleansing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was indicated as being a key element, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In that statement a report was made in July 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: May this exhibit be marked next in order, please? (To the witness): Dr. Greve, do you recognise that document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is an appeal made by the International Committee of the Red Cross to all parties in the conflict in Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is the date of that document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is dated 13th August 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that among the details made available to the Commission?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I tender that exhibit into evidence, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Is there any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Exhibit 76 will be admitted. MR. TIEGER (To the witness): In its press release of that date, does the ICRC report that it had visited places of detention in Bosnia and Herzegovina and that it was evident that innocent civilians were being arrested and subjected to inhumane treatment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did it further state that the detention of such persons was part of a policy of forced population transfers carried out on a massive scale, and marked by the systematic use of brutality, including such methods as harassment, murder, confiscation of property, deportation and the taking of hostages, all in violation of international law?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: May this document be marked for identification next, your Honour? (To the witness): Dr. Greve, do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is it, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is a declaration on Bosnia-Herzegovina issued by the CSO, meaning the Committee of Senior Officials, and it is to be found within the body CSCE, meaning the then conference, now Organisation, on Security and Co-operation in Europe.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it among the reports that prompted the Resolution of 780 and that was made available to the Commission?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was made available to the Commission, yes. I do not know exactly which document the Security Council had at hand when they decided.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is the date of this declaration?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is 12th May 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would tender this document.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Exhibit 77 will be admitted. MR. TIEGER (To the witness): Dr. Greve, in this declaration of May 12th 1992, does the CSO condemn a pattern of clear gross and uncorrected violations of CSCE commitments by the authorities in Belgrade and the JNA, and declare that they bear the prime responsibility for the escalation of bloodshed and destruction in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does the declaration of May 12th 1992 further state in paragraph 5, and emphasise, that the JNA must end its aggression, and does it further insist that the JNA in Bosnia-Herzegovina must either be withdrawn, disarmed or subject to the authority of the government in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is also correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Dr. Greve, in addition to information collated and received pursuant to resolution 780, did the Commission, in fact, actively seek information from other sources?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the Commission sought information from any possible source we could think of.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In addition to evaluating and analysing the materials, the substantiated information, submitted by humanitarian organisations, and actively seeking out information that led to the conflict as a whole, did any member of the Commission focus on any particular area of the conflict?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, some of us did -- I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What area of the conflict did you focus on?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I had asked to focus on a relatively small area for the reason that I joined the Commission relatively late. I had not asked to focus on any specific area, but it ended up being opstina Prijedor in north western Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did you seek to focus on a particular area of the conflict?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was asked by the Commission to look at detention facilities, torture and sexual abuse. It was not clear when I joined the Commission if it would have to finish its work within two and a half months, six and a half months, or nine and a half months and I thought, in order to be able to do anything of value, I should try to limit my focus.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why was Prijedor, in fact, selected as your particular area of focus?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Actually, I had suggested myself that possibly I could focus on Stupni Do. However, it so happened that the Commission was approached by Swedish authorities who communicated they had made numerous interviews with survivors living in Sweden, and since my mother tongue, Norwegian, is close to the Swedish, and the statements were in Swedish, I was asked by the Commission to look at those specific statements.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the availability of these statements present particular opportunity for study of a certain region?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the majority of those who had given statements in Sweden came from opstina Prijedor which at that time was unknown to me. I may, perhaps, add that I worked for the United Nations transitional authorities in Cambodia in the second half of 1992 and beginning of 1993, meaning I was out of Europe when some of the main events happened in the former Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would the study of a particular region permit you to examine the context of alleged war crimes as opposed to a more broad-based evaluation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it did and I thought that would be crucial to meet with my mandate.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there certain advantages presented for your study of the conflict in Prijedor by the fact that witnesses and refugees were scattered around Europe and the world?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I considered that to be extremely important mainly for security reasons and to help me seek for the truth. I thought it would be better to have people interviewed simultaneously in different corners of the world, rather than to go for a few or even some hundred in one refugee centre. I thought it impossible for them to make up stories if they were interviewed very separate.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What methodology was implemented?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The methodology -- it may not sound very professional, I do not think anyone had done this kind of a study before -- I decided I wanted to have interviewed survivors from the area in different countries, and I enlisted in doing that professionals, meaning judges, lawyers, policemen and immigration officers in different countries. It happened in Sweden, it happened in Norway, it happened in Malaysia, it happened in the Netherlands, it happened in Germany and it happened in Croatia at the time the Commission had access to Croatia. So close to 400 people were interviewed in these areas. It was, as mentioned, carried out by people who were selected by the local authorities. We had no resources to pay anyone to do this, so we had to go hat in hand and ask each government to find the people to assist us, which they did. I myself focused on co-ordinating this and searching for other sources of information, meaning that I immediately tried to approach embassies or their intelligence sources, their general sources, their information relating to refugees or evacuees, deportees, perhaps it is better to call them. I started looking for media report and I was very keen on finding local sources. We did approach also the embassies or the representations of the countries involved in the area. We approached, or I arranged it so that we approached, every international agency that had been involved, and other entities of the UN that had been involved -- UNPROFOR is one example. I had had the honour to work with Yasushi Akashi when I was in Cambodia for the United Nations, and many of my old friends were with UNPROFOR. So I had an easy inroad to that. UNHCR were my old colleagues. We approached ICRC and we approached every non-governmental agency that had been working in the area or close to the area as, essentially, there had in the crucial period of time been no-one inside, save for a few local entities such as Merhamet, the Muslim relief agency and Caritas, the Catholic relief agency. I also approached all observers that could be identified to have worked in the area, also from the European Community, and every reporter from the newspaper or television broadcast who had been to the area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you also seek out and obtain information from the media in or around the area of Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And also media from sources from the former Yugoslavia generally?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did and I may, perhaps, since I forgot it, also mention that in a different format and slightly different in nature, we received also witness information from countries such as the United States of America, the United Kingdom, France, Denmark, Switzerland and basic information from a number of countries in addition to that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you yourself go to Prijedor to interview witnesses remaining there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not for very specific reasons. One was at the time the Serbian authorities did not want us to go. I was offered to go, just associate with others and go unofficially. I did not consider that wise as I thought it would be dangerous to people if I spoke to them. I could leave; they could not.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I have this map marked next in order for identification? I understand it is available on the screen as reference No. 237.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: What does that statement mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I am sure of Judge McDonald's view -- it comes from somewhere and it is now on the screen.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: This is exhibit 78, is it not?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: OK. MR. TIEGER (To the witness): Dr. Greve, do you recognise this as a map of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the lower part of the country is left out but, yes, this is, essentially, the whole country.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I tender that for admission, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Is there any objection to 78?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: 78 will be admitted. MR. TIEGER (To the witness): Dr. Greve, let us begin by asking you exactly where Prijedor is.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am not fully familiar with this. I am trying to point it out. Does that help or maybe it does not? Yes, it does with this one, perhaps. Does this reflect on the screen?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, the arrow shows?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Where I put a little arrow is where Prijedor is located, that is, this is the city or the town of Prijedor, and the opstina is quite rectangular in shape, but it is also called Prijedor. It is a larger area. As you can see, your Honours, it is located in the north western corner of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I would ask that Exhibit 57 be shown to the witness. (Document handed). Dr. Greve, this is an exhibit which was shown earlier in the trial. Before I ask you to discuss the conflict in Prijedor in detail, I would like to ask you for a very brief outline of what happened, what took place, in Prijedor. First of all, this exhibit indicates Prijedor, April 30th. What happened in Prijedor, April 30th 1992?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: May I just raise one matter here? I do it because it is important at this stage. Should we not be made aware of the witness's sources as we go through her evidence ---

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: -- as to how is she able to tell us what happened in Prijedor where this information comes from.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Yes, we had agreed, I think. Were you here when Dr. Gow -- when that issue came up?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I am aware of it being mentioned and I think it is important at this stage.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Why not speak to it and then let me suggest a way to approach it. Go ahead, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I thought the ----

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: You can just ask the witness if she knows what happened on April 30th. Then I imagine she will say "yes" and then ask her what is the basis for that knowledge, so that she would then begin to talk, first, about the basis of the knowledge before she gives the opinion. Is there a problem with doing it that way?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: No, not at all, but I would be of the view that that is, essentially, what we just did, was to outline the basis of her knowledge for the events which happened in Prijedor. If the court wishes specific examples as we go through the evidence, certainly we can provide that.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Are you saying then that the response to this question is going to be based upon the methodology that she described?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I think it would be difficult for any expert witness to identify each and every source which converges on particular pieces of information. Certainly, as can you see from the exhibit list, we have quite a number of exhibits identified; specific sources will, therefore, be identified during the course of the presentation. I certainly have no objection to asking the witness at every juncture for the basis of her information but, as I indicated earlier, her testimony today is about those areas where all available information converges to permit her to offer an opinion.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I do not think I am being unduly technical about this and I appreciate the court's ruling earlier this afternoon, but there are still, even within the Tribunal, bounds of admissibility as to what may be acceptable evidence, what may not. We should be told the sources in relation to this testimony as it goes through, so that we know what credit should be given to it, what weight should be given to it. If the court is of the view that this evidence is able to be heard, then the court will have to do a weighing up process in its function as the Tribunal of fact and law to know what value to put upon it.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I agree. I do not think it is necessary for the witness though to repeat every time. I gather her answer would be: "Do you know what happened in Prijedor?" "Yes, I do". "What is the basis of your information?" Then would she would say and she would begin with methodology, I gather, that describes starting at 12 minutes after 3.00, that is, interviewing 400 people and then all of the other reports, talking with reporters, media people, NGOs, UNPROFOR, ICRC and, I gather, that this is what Mr. Tieger is saying he does want her to repeat it every time; if she could do a shorthand version saying, "I followed the same methodology".

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: One of the dangers in wrapping it up is we are not quite sure where the information has come from. If the court is to decide what weight to attribute to this particular evidence, the court may not know where the source is from; whether it is a from a broadcast or from reports of others.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I think it is sufficient if you just ask the witness whether or not or her opinion is based on the methodology that she has described. That is sufficient. OK. MR. TIEGER (To the witness): Dr. Greve, you indicated that you did know what happened in Prijedor on April 30th?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is that based on?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My best source of information as to what happened in Prijedor on 30th April 1992 is an interview given in the local newspaper, Kozarski Vjesnik, about one year later when the head of the then Serbian police was promoted to become Deputy Minister of Interior in the Republika Srpska; his giving a detailed information of that which is corroborating the information I had bits and pieces of previously, and there were also a number of other local Serb officials who have given newspaper interviews on this issue.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is it that did happen in Prijedor on April 30th 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The Serbs were taking power by the use of armed force both as the head of police reports without one bullet fired. They had taken up positions, armed positions, with checkpoints all over the town of Prijedor. They had placed soldiers, armed people, outside all the main buildings, snipers on some roofs and they entered the main buildings to declare that they had taken power in the early morning from approximately 4 o'clock until 6 o' clock in the morning of 30th April 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this takeover by force of arms an act by local Serbs isolated from Serbs outside of opstina Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. It was made in tandem with other Serb entities and that is also addressed by the chief of police himself. He said we worked hand-in-hand. I assume this will be an exhibit later, but in this specific article in a newspaper he is addressing the fact that he worked hand-in-hand, as head of police, with the military and the politicians, and that he was taking instructions from the police headquarters in Banja Luka and also from the Ministry of Interior under which the police sought.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened in Prijedor after the military takeover?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After the military took over, they declared that this had become Srpska opstina Prijedor, meaning the Serbian opstina Prijedor. They did not meet resistance at this point, meaning that most of the population was eager to see if this would continue to be a bloodless takeover. Immediately, however, non-Serbs started to feel that they were being isolated, they lost their jobs, they, essentially, had to stay at home, soon came under curfew, needed passes to travel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Eventually, what happened in opstina Prijedor to the Muslims and Croats of that community?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were basically ousted from the community by violence and armed force, that is, there was a census -- that is my source for numbers -- of 1991, according to which there were approximately 49,000 Muslims in the opstina; the number were reduced to approximately 6,000 within a year's time. There were approximately, again according to the census -- and I may say my source of reference when it comes to the reduced numbers is newspaper article again in Kozarski Vjesnik; it is published in the summer of 1993 and it is addressing how many are we now, it is not saying anything about how the reduction happened -- but then the Croat population was reduced from a little more than 6,000 to a little more than 3,000.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were the Muslims and Croats about whom you have just spoken removed from opstina Prijedor by force of arms, by the establishment of camps and by forced deportation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I think that is a matter for the witness to say. We are in an unusual position here. My learned friend is there putting words into the witness's mouth when she is the expert witness before the court .

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: It is clearly leading, but the problem is how technical are we going to be; this is a bench trial. All three of we judges have tried bench trials for many, many years. In a bench trial, we tend to be more relaxed and, therefore, we allow witnesses sometimes to be led. There is a saying, at least in the American way, you can lead them but please do not drag them, meaning at some point you have to stop. It is a leading question. I think you can just ask the witness what happened, but keep in mind we are not going to tie the witnesses nor counsel to very strict rules because, if we do, it will have to be applied to both sides.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I understand that, your Honour, which is why over the last two weeks we have been extremely quiet here about the leading questions over the last few weeks because we were aware of the issue.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Very good.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: But this was beyond.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: This is leading and an objection has been made. I will sustain the objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Very well, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Ask the witness how they were removed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you. (To the witness): In what way, how were the Muslims and Croats you spoke of earlier removed from opstina Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: For (1) they were not allowed to leave on their own initiative. The area was almost sealed off from the outside world. Then their main settlements were surrounded, bombarded and invaded, after which the women, the children up to 12 or 15, and the elderly men, maybe 60, 65 -- there are various reports on that -- would be separated to be put into one detention camp essentially made for the purpose of deportation. This group was, essentially, deported, and a group of males between 12 or 15 and 60, 65, was put into two detention camps known as Keraterm and Omarska. Keraterm is located in Prijedor, so sometimes it is referred to just as "Prijedor", as a camp, but its name is Keraterm; and we do not know exact numbers but, unfortunately, there are many who never left Prijedor alive. Many were killed in the military attacks and in camps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Dr. Greve, I would like to focus on opstina Prijedor and ask you for some details about the opstina. Let me begin by asking you exactly what an opstina is.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is, perhaps, one of the more difficult questions because I do not think we have an accurate translation; "municipality" or "district", it is an administrative unit in the former Yugoslavia. So possibly calling it a "municipality" or a "district" will be correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that municipality broken down into any smaller administrative units?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is. The next administrative unit is called Mjesna Zajednica. It is a combination of villages, hamlets and in the city, the city as such is slightly subdivided in Mjesna Zajednica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is the approximate size, geographic size, of opstina Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If my memory serves my right, it is 834 square kilometres, according to the statistics.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From one end to the other, approximately how long?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Possibly 33 kilometres by 25 and a half kilometres, but this, obviously, is approximate and the shape is not exactly rectangular but it is almost like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, if could I have these documents marked next in order for identification? (Documents handed).

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: What number is that, Mr. Tieger?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That would be No. 79, I believe it is No. 79. (To the witness): Dr. Greve, do you recognise those documents?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are those two separate documents?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There are actually three different documents. There is one or, that is to say, there is one Serbo-Croatian version of the document and then there is an English language version of the same document, and this has been published by the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina but, unfortunately, it is not so easy to read the figures. So for, as a matter of convenience, I have also asked to have handed a copy of the same population count and census published in Croatia because it is readable. I have been unable to trace a better copy from Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I tender that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: The Prosecution provided with the document number because we do not know.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Is it 79 or is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: That is the exhibit number probably, but what is the original document number?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: What is listed on the exhibit list, 79 is a coloured map of Prijedor and surrounding area taken from a section of the map series M709. Is that what has been marked as 79.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: No, the map has not been marked and 79 has not been assigned to any particular exhibit yet.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I have a feeling it is 80 just from what I have listened to -- no, it is not 80 either.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, if it will be of more convenience to the court, the map will certainly be marked later. I can have the witness identify it now so we can keep the list in order.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: That is fine. Identified. Then 79, does the Defence counsel have a copy of what has been marked for identification purposes as 79?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: I think there is still a little confusion here. Perhaps the Prosecution could give us the document number which you provided to us, because we have three numbers now here, the original document number which may be 2 and 44, but the document number you gave to us had different numbers and these are the references I am working with.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Correct. The document number on the list that you are working with should be numbers 2 ---

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: -- and 44. To keep things in order, if we may have this marked for identification and have the witness look at that.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Tell me what has just been marked as 79.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, what was marked for identification -- I am sorry about the confusion -- were documents 80 and 81 which turned out to be marked as one exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: OK, that is what I thought because I did not think that what the witness added -- she was saying there were three pieces of paper and I could not see that was a colour map and that is what you have listed as 79. OK. MR. TIEGER (To the witness): Judge Greve, looking quickly at the document that has just been marked, do you recognise that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is it, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is the central areas of opstina Prijedor. It was difficult to have the entire opstina into the map for the form I have wanted, but it is the essential parts of opstina Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I tender that.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: That has been marked as what number for identification?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I was hoping it had been -- 79.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: 79, and it is listed on your exhibit list as a coloured map of Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Does Defence counsel have any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: No, I understand now we have changed this into 79 and the other document will be 80, is that correct, because I was under the impression that the document had been given 79, but that is wrong?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If I may clarify, if we may mark the census from the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina states statistics office which has the English translation as Exhibit 80, and the census that the witness indicated was obtained from Croatia with the same information but in clearer form as 81, then we will be back on the court's list.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: 79 being the map, no objection, and 80 being the census 1991, no objection either.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: 79 will be admitted, the coloured map of Prijedor and surrounding area, and 80 will be admitted also without objection, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. Your Honours, it might make things clearer if we go through the evidence to mark though two censuses as 80.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: 81 on your exhibit list says pages 196 through 201 report from a report of 1991 census, is that what 81 is?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Is there any objection to 81?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: 81 will be admitted. 79, 80 and 81 are admitted. The hard part is over. Now we can listen to the testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. Can this document be marked as No. 82? That comes up on the screen as 2/40. It is an ethnic composition map of opstina Prijedor. (To the witness): Dr. Greve, do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is a map which shows the majority ethnic group in the different areas. Unfortunately, this is not in colours; it would be much more readable if that was the case.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It shows the ethnic composition of opstina Prijedor by the different towns or villages?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honours, as Judge Greve indicated, this is a copy of the original which has been on its way for sometime. I would ask to tender this with the understanding that the original colour document will be provided to the court and a colour copy to the Defence as soon as available which, I hope, will be later today.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Any objection -- you have 82, I think, before you -- to 82 ---

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: -- subject to the original in colour being presented?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: No problem.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: 82 will be admitted. MR. TIEGER (To the witness): Dr. Greve, can you tell us the approximate national or ethnic distribution or composition of the Prijedor area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Prijedor, according to the census of 1991, had a little more than 112,000 inhabitants. The number of inhabitants was increased, we do not know exactly by how many, but by summer in early 1992 because of ethnic cleansing practices in Bosanski Novi, which will be to the west, almost only to the west, of opstina Prijedor. In opstina Prijedor, the Muslims had the majority population. They were 44 per cent of the entire population which means approximately 49,000 people; the Serbs were 42.5 per cent of the population; the Croats were 5.6 per cent of the population, and there was a group that deserves a little explanation called Yugoslavs which was 5.7 per cent. Yugoslavs were used as a designation. It was an option for everyone to declare themselves as Yugoslavs, and it was chosen for primarily two options. That is my understanding. If people were of mixed descent, although that did not prevent them from also declaring them belonging to one or the other group, and the other reason for calling oneself a Yugoslav would be demonstrating political confidence in the idea of Yugoslavia as one state. There was finally a group of 2.2 per cent which were aliens. They are, according to the public records, essentially, Ukrainians, Russians and Italians. However, to my understanding, there has also been some, not so many, but Albanians, and some, not so many, Poles, or there could have been others as well. I may mention that gypsies do not figure on this account, but that is one of the groups that has also been ousted from the region, but I have not seen -- or from opstina Prijedor, but I have never see official numbers as to how many they were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could the witness be shown this map for identification next in order? It will be No. 83, I believe. (Document handed). Dr. Greve, do you recognise that map?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What does it depict?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This particular map is to indicate the division between ethnic groups. I hasten to add that such a division is not always easy to make as many people find it difficult to identify only with one group, as they are of mixed descent. In many areas up to one-fourth of the marriages were between Christian and Muslims. But, however, this is according to how people had declared themselves in the census. So, by giving the different groups a colour code, meaning that the Croats are marked with blue, the Muslims with green and the Serbs in some kind of reddish shade -----

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Dr. Greve, before you go further, I would like to tender that exhibit and put it on the monitor so the court can see it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am sorry.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Is there objection to 83?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: No objection, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: 83 will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Dr. Greve, can you point out on the map where opstina Prijedor appears?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, long distance reading is not my strong side, but I will try to do it properly. This is Prijedor with the 44 per cent Muslims and the 42.5 per cent Serbs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is the ethnic or national distribution of the opstina surrounding Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Most of the opstinas surrounding Prijedor has more than half of the population as being Serb. One will see immediately that there are some exceptions such as Sanski Most, and I am trying to find Kotor Varos which is also one such opstina which does not have Serb majority population. I am leaving out at this time the Bihac area which I was trying to point out in the corner -- I do not know if you, it is not on my screen; oh, yes, here it is -- which is predominantly a Muslim area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, doctor. I would like to ask you some questions about the general geographic position of Prijedor. In that regard, I would like the witness to be shown the next exhibit to be marked for identification which should be Exhibit 84. While they are setting that up, perhaps you could just take a look at the document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I have been colouring it myself so I think I do know it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you recognise that document, what does it depict?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is a document which was issued by the British forces in UNPROFOR as of 17th February 1993. It shows the current military situation at that time, but it is of no significance, neither the time, nor the military situation. My main reason for asking this map to be used is that it shows both Serbia proper with Vojvodina, it shows Montenegro and it shows essential parts of Croatia, that is, the four UN protected areas in Croatia and all of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: We tender Exhibit 84, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: No objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: 84 will be admitted. MR. TIEGER (To the witness): Dr. Greve, now that the map is in front of the court, can you point out the areas you refer to, both Prijedor and Serbia and Serbia and Krajina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know if it will be of convenience if I stand up or if you cannot hear me then, but I -----

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: That be a problem when you stand up. See if you can point from sitting down, if you can.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Let me say, for the record, there is no political colour to the yellow; it was the highlighter at hand. This is the borderline which indicates where we find Serbia proper, Montenegro, Serbia and Vojvodina. All that is east of this line could well have been coloured yellow. What we see here is it is marked east, west, north and south. These are the UN protected areas in Croatia following the cease fire in early 1992. I have coloured them in full to show just how large the areas are. My main reason for making this map is to draw the attention of your Honours to the fact that to link this yellow eastern area to this yellow tree, well, in actual fact, two areas in the west, there is a need for some kind of passage or territorial infrastructure link. I may point out that this is central Bosnia. This is where we find Sarajevo. This is where, sort of, the government in Bosnia-Herzegovina was predominantly in control. This area, as pointed out, had a predominantly Serb population, not Prijedor, not Sanski Most, not Kotor Varos. However, and there were predominant Serb areas in this stretch as well. To link Serbia proper to these areas, there was a need for some kind of a corridor or sometimes the reference to a "corridor" in written sources, meaning newspaper article and when referred to by the military, may be limited to the area of Brcko, opstina Brcko, Bosanski Samac, which you have had witnesses coming in from. In this area, the so-called corridor was very narrow. However, in this area it was quite broad but to get through immediately, not having control of Prijedor, was an obstacle in terms of infrastructure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Dr. Greve, is there a major highway which connects substantial portions of areas you have just been pointing to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, actually Prijedor has a character of an intersection in this respect. Obviously, it is much more than an intersection, but also that it links the most important town in the area which is Banja Luka over to Bosanski Novi. It goes straight through Prijedor. It links Bosanski Dubica to Banja Luka through Prijedor, or to Bosanski Novi through Prijedor, or to Sanski Most to the south. So, it literally is an intersection between the four cardinal directions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is there also a railroad which links some of those areas?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is. The railroad in this area goes straight through Prijedor coming again from the west or from the east, depending where you start, of course. It goes straight through Prijedor and onwards to Banja Luka, and onwards to Duboj. It is the only one railroad in that area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this passageway from Serbia to Serbian Krajina that you have just indicated considered important by Serbian officials and authorities?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is being referred to as if it is the neck, that links the head and the body. It is referred to as the vital line of life. It is referred to as the crucial point to have one unified territory or united link, geographical territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: May I have this marked next in order, please, for identification. (Document marked) (To the witness): Dr. Greve, do you recognise that document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell the court what it is, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is the original and a translation of an article which appeared 1st June 1994 in the local newspaper in opstina Prijedor, the local newspaper called Kozarski Vjesnik, and the headline of the article is "The Glory of all Serbian glories".

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After the military takeover in Prijedor on April 30th 1992, was Kozarski Vjesnik an independent newspaper?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, it was not. Kozarski Vjesnik immediately became almost a mouth piece of the new authorities.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would tender that document.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: 85 will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: May I ask it to be placed on the elmo and the witness's attention directed to page 2, the last paragraph.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I am sorry, Mr. Tieger, I missed -- what paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: The last paragraph of page 2, your Honours, which begins, "Loyal followers of Serbian heros". (To the witness): Dr. Greve, do you see in that paragraph a reference to the significance placed by Serbian authorities on the passageway between Serbia proper and Serbian Krajina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do. It is said in the operation to open the so-called, and in quotation mark "corridor", "that natural and generic (sic) ... of the Serbs in all three Serbian states, the fight is from ... supported by institutions of civil authority and the Serbian people proved that they were loyal followers of Serbian heros from all previous wars and battles ... beginning with the Kosovo battle until now".

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is attached from a telegram sent by whom?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is sent by the Regional Commander, General Momir Talic who is headquartered in Banja Luka. He is the Commander of the 1st Krajina corps which previously has been referred to under its JNA name by previous witnesses as being the Fifth Krajina or the Banja Luka due to its headquarters. .

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I think that the witness when she was reading the "natural and genetic" I think she said "generic".

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Only because I think it is a significance to have pointed out. We will stand in recess for 20 minutes. (4.00 o'clock). (Short adjournment). (4.20 p.m.).

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. Your Honour, before I begin I just wanted, if I may, to clarify a question that Judge Stephen asked me earlier that I entirely missed. It was about a reference number I made to a computer exhibit. I did mention a number. It is my understanding that that is the identification number for the document which has already been scanned into the computer. So, if reference is made in the course of the examination to 2/ and then a number, I think that typically refers to an exhibit that has already been scanned into the computer. I am sorry I misunderstood the question. Dr. Greve ----

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: While you are on this, I suppose it is too much to hope that we can get coloured maps of any of these exhibits? Our copies I suspect will all be black and white, will they?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: For some of the maps we have prepared duplicate colour copies for the Court, especially the map, for example, one of the maps that has already been introduced. I will get the number and perhaps it would be a good time to give a copy to the court, Exhibit 79. I am happy to present that now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: As the Doctor has said, it is probably very much easier to understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I am sure it will be possible and we will make an effort to do that for all relevant exhibits.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Dr. Greve, before the break we were discussing the passageway through from Serbia to Serbia and Krajina, and the significance of that passageway to Serbian officials. In that connection you referred to a telegram from General Talic. I would ask you now to look at a document I would like marked for identification as Exhibit 86. What is that document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is another article from Kozarski Vjesnik. I see that unfortunately it is called Publication 02 Vjesnik. I assume this is a mistake. It is Kozarski Vjesnik, the local newspaper which we have been referring to previously. It is dated 15th July 1994, headline: "Faithful to the Homeland and its Ideals".

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does it contain the text of a speech by the chairman of the Prijedor SDS?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it does, and that is the Serbian party.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was that speech made at a ceremony commemorating the birth of the party?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I tender that Exhibit, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Any objection to Exhibit 86?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: No objection, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: 86 will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Dr. Greve, directing your attention to page 3 of the English translation, the second paragraph, in his speech does the President of the Prijedor SDS indicate the significance that is attached to the passageway between Serbia and Serbia and Krajina by Serbian officials?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how does he describe that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It said: "The word 'corridor' is too weak to describe that bond. The neck is not a corridor between the head and the body; it is all one being, the being of the Serbian nation, said the top man of the Prijedor SDS categorically."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does Prijedor lie right in the midst of that single body?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Speaking in the language of a body, it is like a heart in the middle of this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now is an opportunity for me to refer to the computer document 235 once more. May that be called up on the screen? I am sorry, your Honour, I would like to ask that Exhibit 79 be placed on the elmo. Dr. Greve, looking at this map of Prijedor, can you point out for the court the major population centres of the opstina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. The only larger town is Prijedor itself which is located here; somehow in the middle but rather to the west than the east of the opstina. Then there are some other main population areas. One is underneath the mountain range that we find to the north where the central areas are actually Kozarac and Kozarusa.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I can barely see that. Can you zoom on it just a little bit more, Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Here we see Kozarac. Again frequently, as earlier mentioned, the administrative unit is Mjesna Zajednica which is slightly bigger than each area, and frequently one will also refer to an area as the "Kozarac area" or Podgozara, meaning a larger area. But this is Kozarac proper. Maybe I should point out there is one main road from Prijedor that goes the way to Banja Luka. This is a new road and there is an old road. These are the two roads crossing through Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Is that what is labelled 4 and it appears to be that road?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is the newest road and that leads from Prijedor. It is also called E for European, main road E761. The old road is called 13 just to the north, this being the main centre of Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Approximately how many people lived in the general Kozarac region?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If we take the entire region, but again it depends on how we want to make the limits to that, but it may be said that almost 27,000 people lived in the larger Kozarac area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the general ethnic composition of that area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was predominantly and more than that essentially Muslim.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Dr. Greve, can you tell us a little about some of the major industries or economic activities of the opstina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Maybe if I can take the liberty, I had not finished pointing out some of the main centres. Maybe I confused by being so slow in presenting them, but I would like to point out to the court also the area of Ljubija. We are moving the map and what we are actually seeing now is an area which is to the west and the south of the Prijedor town; it is called Ljubija. That is also one of the main population centres in the opstina, the third largest one. Then coming back to your question, Prijedor as mentioned is located at an intersection. So there were a lot of passage traffic and transport that was allocated to the area. The main industry in the area, this is a mountainous areas, your Honours, and the main industry is an iron ore mine. It is believed to be possibly the second largest in Europe both in quantity and quality. So, it is a large mine and Ljubija is one of the mining centres. We have not touched upon the two other main centres or locations of the mine. It has three locations, one being Omarska and a third being Tomasica. In the middle of the focus at the moment you also see some other industries actually. You will see that there is a clay production plant; it is also known under the name of Keraterm. There were a number of sawmills, timber, paper mills, biscuit factory, soft drink factory, some textile factories. It was considered a prosperous area. It is fertile. It is with quite some agricultural activity, animal husbandry and forestry. It is underneath the mountain of Kozara. The Kozara mountain holds significant importance in the history of the former Yugoslavia during World War II. So, possibly the single most important war memorial in the former Yugoslavia is on top of this mountain. There were a lot of tourists coming to the area, both to visit the memorial and also because it has a pleasant climate and a pleasant location with the River Sana, as opposed to the River Sava. The River Sana runs through the opstina. It comes from the west. It comes almost all the way down to Prijedor to the town, and it continues to the south. So Prijedor, in a sense, is in a valley setting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In addition to Kozarski Vjesnik, was there any other local media outlet?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Radio Prijedor was the local radio station.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Dr. Greve, you indicated that there were three primary ethnic groups or nationalities in Prijedor. How were relations between those groups between World War II and the late 1980s or 1990?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To my understanding, it was very good relations between the different ethnic groups, to the extent that one is surprised to read local newspaper articles where Serb officials will actually say that they abandoned the brotherhood that existed, and it comes through -- and this is of course an impression which I have having seen all the witness statements -- that people were really surprised that anything like this could happen in Prijedor, because it was an early partisan area and it suffered terribly during World War II. This was an area in which later United Nations Secretary General Kurt Waldheim worked during World War II. So a lot of intelligence work has been made as to what happened in the Prijedor area in World War II. It was heavily decimated in the summer of 1942 and all groups suffered tremendously. Obviously the destruction of the area was led by the Germans, their Austrian allies, Kurt Waldheim being an Austrian, the Ustasha, the fascist of the Croatians, but also the Serb Chetniks had been cleared as being useful in co-operating in this. It so comes that in my own country, and I checked these sources in my country and in Belgrade just to get some indication of World War II history, unfortunately many people from Prijedor were taken to Jasanovac which is a terrible concentration camp during World War II, possibly the worst in the former Yugoslavia, but some of them were also taken for slave labour in my own country. So I have looked up the lists of those taken for slave labour in occupied Norway, and among them are many Serbs, but also Muslims from the Prijedor area. So there is a constant reference in every media to the "brotherhood" of the past. They had suffered together and it seems like so many have been sort of emphasising in this case that they really considered one another as living together harmoniously.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this harmonious relationship which existed for so long after World War II suddenly shattered on April 30th or 1992 or did it build up over time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It did build up over time and not the least due to massive propaganda and the upcoming nationalistic trends, but essentially, I hasten to add, outside of Prijedor, but the population in Prijedor became subjected to ethnic hatred, particularly from Serbian medias.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: May I have this document marked for identification as No. 87?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the middle of marking the document maybe I should also point out something I forgot. There seems to be a lake on the map, Ridna. This is actually not just an ordinary lake; this is a huge fish farm, fish plant. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Looking at document 87, can you tell us what that is, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. This is a General Assembly, Security Council document in the UN. It is circulated by both of them. It relates to the situation on human rights in the territory of the former Yugoslavia. It is the Secretary General that presents to the General Assembly and the Security Council a report concerning the situation of human rights in the territory of the former Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I tender that document, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: No objection, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: 87 will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Dr. Greve, can I direct your attention to page 10 of that document and ask you if it indicates the role of the media in areas controlled by de facto Bosnian Serb authorities?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you reviewed that previously?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I note that the report was made in 1995.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does the assessment of the situation at that time reflect the role of the media at the time in 1991/1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To my understanding, it reflects the situation even better in 1991 and 1992 than in 1995, because in 1995 the need for propaganda was not that important.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now in which way does this report indicate the media in areas controlled by de facto Bosnian Serb authorities attempted to influence the population?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is indicating that instead of brotherhood there is an upcoming rivalry and worse between the different groups. It is starting to characterise the Croatians as Ustashas and fascists, and it is starting to categorise the Muslims and fundamentalists, people wanting to rage holy war, "Jihad", that is it is presenting a scenario which seems to leave no other options for the Serbs than to join some kind of self-defence against all other groups or possibly face this terrible fate of the past, that is concentration camps such as Jasanovac. It seems to be made an either/or.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In paragraph 38 does the report indicate that the Bosnian Serb authorities in essence created their own media for the purpose of disseminating political propaganda?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In paragraph 40 the report makes reference to broadcasts which refer to President Itzebegovic as "balija". Is that an ethnic insult?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is considered to be very derogative, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The report indicates that that was done on the Bosnian Serb media?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: May I ask you to turn to paragraph 43. Now the early reference that you discussed talked about the creation of a Bosnian Serb media. Does this paragraph indicate the manner in which that media in some ways was created?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. It is referring to certain existing medias being taken over, the control of these medias being taken over by the Bosnian Serbs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: May I have this document marked as Exhibit 88 for identification? (Document handed). Doctor, do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is it, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is a transcript of a broadcast made by Radio TV Banja Luka situated in Banja Luka, being the so-called "Captain" of the region.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I tender this document.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Any objection to Exhibit 88?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Exhibit 88 will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Dr. Greve, let me direct your attention to page 1 of that transcript of the broadcast. What is the occasion which this broadcast marks?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It marks a celebration of the takeover of the TV relay station on mount Kozarac which was taken over by the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The broadcast indicates that the takeover occurred when?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 1st August 1991, but it also indicates, and I think that speaks to a question perhaps previously raised by the Defence, when it comes to information such as the takeover of a TV station, I had information from many witnesses which was not very precise, but when I tried to figure out exactly when this was taken over, I had the answer in this TV or this celebrating that has been broadcast, because people told me or witnesses had testified or given information that they recognised the takeover of the TV station actually by approximately March 1992. What this document tells us is that the actual takeover was 1st August the previous year, but they did not start with Serb dominated information or propaganda immediately. It refers to 28 months. If I may, for your convenience, draw your attention to the first paragraph because this is a three-year celebration in a sense but it is only 28 months that it has been operational. So, this document tells how bits and pieces of information sometimes would not give me the complete picture, but eventually more and more documents would come up to corroborate the information. I had put it into a more precise context.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Looking at paragraph 3, does the broadcast indicate who captured the transmitter?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is a paramilitary group. I do not see it immediately on my transcript in paragraph 3, but it is a group that called themselves the Wolves. They come from Panjavo or Vukia which is a mountain in Panjavo. Panjavo is an opstina located to the east of Prijedor, east of Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does the broadcast indicate who came with the armed group, again looking at paragraph 3 which start with "Reporter"? I direct your attention to the quote which begins "Around 1800 hours ... " Perhaps I am directing your attention to the wrong portion, Doctor. The third paragraph that begins "Reporter", do you see a reference to "1800 hours"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. "Around 1800 hours today officials of the Bosanski Krajina SO Municipal Assembly came to the centre with a large armed escort and ordered us to broadcast the satellite programme from Belgrade via the second relay". It is indicating that this was not the paramilitary forces acting on their own. They were actually acting in tandem with, and full co-operation of, both army and political leaders.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does the President of the autonomous region of Krajina appear in the broadcast to celebrate the takeover of the transmitter?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is his name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is Kupresanin

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does the broadcast and does he indicate in the broadcast that the takeover of the transmitter took place under his orders?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he does.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is there any official from Prijedor present at the celebration?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Turning to the top of page 2 -- let me ask you first to direct your attention to the bottom of page 1, if I may. That indicates Srdo Srdic Deputy in the People's Assembly in the Republic of Srpske. Do you know from which opstina Srdo Srdic comes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He lived at least in opstina Prijedor. I do not know if he was also born there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the time of the takeover of the transmitter, was he a member of SDS and where did he live?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He lived in opstina Prijedor, and he was a member of the SDS, and he was an early deputy or representative in the People's Assembly of Republika Srpska which, understandably, had a different name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Turning to the first paragraph of page 2, and looking at the last sentence of that paragraph, does Srdo Srdic indicate why the takeover occurred and when the transmitter was taken over?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he is emphasising that it is a need for propaganda to be transmitted to the Serbian people.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, if we could play the video? Actually, I would ask to have the video of that transcript from which that transcript is taken tendered into evidence before we play it or afterwards.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: That is exhibit 89. Is there any objection to the video, Mr. Wladimiroff?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Exhibit 89 will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That is tape No. 1. (Tape No. 1 was played) Could we hold that for just a moment? I apologise. Your Honour, I apologise. I realised belatedly that the court does not have copies of the transcript before it.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: No, we do not.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: We have two copies at the moment, if that would be convenient for the court? Actually, three copies, if the Defence has no objection; one is marked.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: We can use two copies. How many pages is this exhibit, Mr. Tieger, the transcript, 88?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Four, your Honour. If I recall correctly, we have just stopped at the portion that would have been marked "caption", if the court wishes to continue rather than rewind it. We have just concluded the anchor giving the introductory portion. I think we stopped at the logo. We can continue. (Tape No. 1 continued) Dr. Greve, in addition to inciting hatred against Muslims and Croats by the use of such terms as referred to in the Masowieski Report, did the Bosnian Serb media under the control of the de facto authorities attempt to instil or inspire Serbian nationalism?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In what sorts of ways was that done?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Several different ways. Nationalism as it is coming up, unfortunately, in many parts of Europe; it was inspired by going back to historic events. For (1) there was a celebration of a 600 anniversary of the Battle of Kosovo Polje in 1989, and it was made a big issue that the Serb nation was let down by other people in the area when the Turks, the Ottoman Empire, were able to invade this part of Europe. They were referring to the glorious past; they were referring to religious symbols and they were also, in particular, emphasising that there could be quite a threat to the Serbs as a nation if they did not stick together as they could be subjected to new attack by other national groups, with specific reference then to the Croatians and with the slogan "the Ustasha" which was for good reasons, very good reasons, useful in terms of instilling fear. They were also with this general reference to some fundamentalist, politicized Muslim communities elsewhere and, essentially, outside Europe referring to the Muslims as being possibly a threat to the existence of the Serb nation. This also happened -- maybe I am jumping slightly in terms of time, but as soon as disintegration of the former Yugoslavia start, it is being presented so that if for any one reason Serbs would become a minority population, which they had not been used to in new independent states, their whole existence could be very perilous and endangered.
