So it was made for many people as if they had no choice but a full scale war against everyone else, or to be subjected to the old type concentration camp, the symbol being "Jasanovac".

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the effect of this propaganda? Was it effective?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was extremely effective, and I think that many, many people, having been subjected to this for a long period of time, repeatedly and frequently in very skilled manners, they really were frightened; they were thinking: "Possibly, possibly, something is building up. I do not see it because I am so friendly with my neighbours and relatives, but possibly outside this area, I must be alert to it", and it was very cleverly done and they were afraid and I think it is genuine.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Can I ask that this document be marked for identification as Exhibit 90? (To the witness): What does this document contain, Dr. Greve?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This document is a short quotation which I used for my Prijedor study analysing the events in Prijedor I have found in the historian Noel Malcolm's book entitled, "Bosnia, a short history", which was printed in 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I tender this.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Any objection to Exhibit 90?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: No objection, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Exhibit 90 will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I may, perhaps, take this opportunity to say that within the -----

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Excuse me, I am sorry, can I ask you to put that on the elmo so the court could see it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sure. No, it was not common to the document, but the fact that I am using reference to an historian. I tried to approach every historian whom I came across or had the possibility to get in touch with throughout my study, any nationality, any background, any sign to the conflict.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Directing your attention to Mr. Malcolm's quote, does he indicate that he has attempted to assess the effective propaganda based on his wide travels in Bosnia over 15 years?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he does.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And his review of radio/television Belgrade during period 1991 to 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, he is saying that he thought the coexistence between the groups were very friendly but that the propaganda, unfortunately, was very efficient.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So his experience over a 15 year period was that the country was not seething with ethnic hatred?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But, having watched radio/television Belgrade, he began to understand what had happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What does he say about that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He is actually saying that it is understandable under the circumstances that the local population really became afraid.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does he quote an independent Belgrade journal itself to try to put it in context?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he does. He is quoting a journalist called Milos Vacic(?) and he is -- who is making an allusion to the American context. Did you want me to read it? Yes? "You must imagine a United States with every little TV station everywhere taking exactly the same editorial line, a line dictated by David Duke. You too would have war in five years", and then the reference is to the Ku Klux Klan.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Dr. Greve, I would like you to take a look at this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VOHRAH
utterances.text: Dr. Greve, who is David Duke? I am not American so I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may? He was a neo-Nazi or very extreme right wing racist, political leader from Louisiana who came perilously close to obtaining some higher officer in Louisiana.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VOHRAH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Can the witness be shown Exhibit 85, please? Can you put page 1 on the elmo, please? (To the witness): Dr. Greve, this article concerns what event in opstina Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is a celebration, the day and glory of the Army of Republika Srpska. It is also orthodox church holiday, St. Vitus.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you had a chance to review the entire article?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Previously, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does it contain examples of the type of propaganda that you were speaking of earlier?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me direct your attention to paragraph 2 which begins "Today". First of all, looking at the line above, can you tell who was speaking?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I assume it will be Radmilo Zeljaja or is it .....

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me ask you this: were both the Commanders of the Prijedor Brigades present at the celebration?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they were. Pero Colic as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The article indicates that they both spoke and are quoted in this article?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is my understanding.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In this first quote, if you look to the bottom of the paragraph which begins "But our honourable noblemen", can you see who is speaking?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I only see a reference to Colonel Radmilo Zeljaja.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is it that Colonel Zeljaja said at that celebration?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Again it is going back to something briefly mentioned earlier. Prince Lassa(?) is one of the three saints and historically important people in the Serbian nation of whom they are duly very proud. Prince Lassa was fighting the battle on behalf of the Serbs at Kosovo Polje which was formed in 1389. Now, it is referred to as 605 years ago.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So this is one example of the promotion of Serbian nationalism you have referred to earlier?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: OK. That would include the reference to Prince Lassa, the reference to Serb noblemen, empire and destiny as well as the characterization of the Serbs as the most tolerant and greatest people on the entire planet?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is a very mixed article, if I may say so, because, of course, it is making reference to points of history of which the Serbs have every reason to be proud and to remember, and not the same as in the Far East, but also in Europe, we have this long tradition of going back for hundreds and hundreds of years and in this sense, perhaps, 600 years is not that much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is Colonel Colic, the Commander of 5th Kozara Brigade also quoted as speaking at the celebration?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does he focus on the threat presented to Serbian people and their potential imperilment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that a reference to, in part, the history you described earlier?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is. It also has an unfortunate reference to this as being the Third World War.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can I direct your attention to page 2, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Is there participation in this celebration at least by telegram by General Ratko Mladic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does he refer to the efforts made by the military forces in the Prijedor area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he does.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How does he refer to those efforts?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: "Up to now our army has managed to successfully protect the Serbian population from the extermination which had been planned, liberated the greatest parts of the Serb land and made it possible for the Serbs in these areas to take their destiny into their hands for the first time".

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does he congratulate them in the second paragraph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he does.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And recognise their achievements and then does he invite them to do something?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he does.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: "... invite you to persist in achieving your freedom and the creation of a unified Serbian state by maintaining a high level of combat readiness of our units and safeguarding our front lines and through strong moral and unity of the people and army, and I wish St. Vitus Day to be celebrated in peace in the years to come."

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: What is the date on this?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: June 1st, 1994.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I wondered, for the record, could you just tell us what St. Vitus Day -- what is that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is my understanding, but I have not been able to have this -- I actually checked through the embassies to have a proper calendar of the different religious feasts -- but it is the day when they celebrate svet knez Lazar being the Prince Lazar, and it maybe that St. Vitus is actually a reference to him. But now I am guessing. I am afraid I am not fully able to help you in this, but it is celebrated the same day.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Dr. Greve, directing your attention once more to page 1.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: The same day that the Turks defeated the -----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: 1589 or something? No.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I must also humbly admit I do not know history that well that I know this.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: That is OK.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Looking at the last line of the first page, is there a reference to the brotherhood that once existed in the Prijedor area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is. The last line actually says, or the last sentence: "We will win because we have firmly decided not to live any longer in brotherhood with those who slaughter our children and with false brothers who have spat several times at Serbian goodness and decency".

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, doctor. Your Honour, I know time has been a consideration, but I am moving on to a separate topic.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Then we will adjourn until tomorrow at 10 a.m. (5.30 p.m.)

procedural_notes.text: (The hearing adjourned for a short time)
(The hearing adjourned until the following day)
